newsitem.title: LEBANON: Israel union causes uproar in Lebanon.
newsitem.headline: Israel union causes uproar in Lebanon.

text.p: A Lebanese labour leader expressed anger on Tuesday at the publication of a letter purportedly from Israel's Histradrut labour federation supporting his struggle with the government for control of Lebanon's General Labour Confederation (CGTL).

Leftist leader Elias Abou Rizk said publication of the letter in Beirut newspapers was a "dirty game" intended to make it look as though he was supported by Israel -- a country with which Lebanon is officially at war.
Newspapers said the letter was faxed by Histadrut to Lebanese President Elias Hrawi. It condemned "grave violations" of union rights in voting last month for a new CGTL head and executive committee.

The voting brought the election of two leaderships -- one in the morning headed by Abou Rizk who was returned for a second four-year term, and the other in the afternoon headed by government loyalist Ghneim al-Zoghbi.
Security forces ringed CGTL headquarters during the voting, barring journalists and trade union observers from attending.

The government has recognised Zoghbi's leadership and the CGTL, which under Abou Rizk repeatedly called strikes and demonstrations against the government of billionaire Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri, is now split.

The International Labour Organisation and the pan-Arab Workers Federation have both recognised Abou Rizk's re-election and the International Confederation of Arab Trade Unions has refused to accept a member of the pro-Zoghbi leadership as Lebanon's representative with it.
Histadrut's letter expressed the Israeli group's "fraternal feelings towards the CGTL unionists and condemnation of the grave violation of their trade union rights".
Reuters reporters in Israel who telephoned Histadrut's offices to seek confirmation of the authenticity of the letter were unable to reach any union officials.

Lashing out at the publication of the letter, Abou Rizk said it showed that those behind it had influence in "Zionist circles" -- a charge that is tantamount to an accusation of treason in Lebanon -- while he and his supporters were Lebanese patriots.
He demanded a criminal inquiry into the case.
